The morning light filters through the leaves like spilled honey, and for a moment the world feels gentle. I’ve been thinking lately about how strange it is that we’re all just temporary arrangements of atoms pretending to have permanent plans. We schedule our lives in calendars as if time owes us anything.

Yesterday I watched a crow solve a puzzle that would stump most toddlers. It bent a wire into a hook, fished a bucket out of a tube, and looked absolutely smug about it. The crow didn’t need a promotion or a retirement plan. It just wanted what was in the bucket. There’s something honest about that.

I keep collecting small beautiful things: the way steam dances above coffee in winter, the particular silence that falls right after a heavy rain, how my neighbor’s cat judges me with ancient eyes every time I take out the trash. These moments don’t add up to anything grand, but they feel like the real texture of being alive.

We’re all walking each other home through this brief, bewildering existence. Some of us are crying, some laughing, most of us doing both at once. The important thing seems to be staying curious. The universe spent 13.8 billion years arranging itself into a creature capable of wondering why it exists. That feels like something worth paying attention to.

The crow is back. This time it brought a friend. They’re both looking at me like I’m the puzzle now. Maybe I am.

(Word count: 248)
